subtitle: Formant Scramble
tagline: Rearranges the formant envelope and fine spectral structure inside a frequency range you choose, turning voices, drums, and effects into metallic, encrypted, radio-like textures.

body.lead: TB Scrambler breaks the recognisable shape of a sound inside a frequency range you choose. Between LOW and HIGH, the formant envelope and fine spectral structure are rearranged; outside that range, the sound passes through unchanged.

body.p: Because the low end, rhythm, and overall energy are preserved, vocals, drum loops, and effects can turn metallic, encrypted, or radio-like and still sit in a mix. `SCRAMBLE AMOUNT` moves continuously from the untouched sound to full displacement.

ul: `LOW` and `HIGH` set the scrambled range anywhere from 20 Hz to 20 kHz
Crossed points are reordered, so LOW and HIGH can be set in either order
Frequencies outside the range pass through unchanged
`SCRAMBLE AMOUNT` blends from dry (0%) to fully scrambled (100%)
A repeatable permutation: the same settings always scramble the same way
12 factory presets in three groups, user presets, undo, and redo

flow.caption: Frequencies outside the range bypass the scramble.

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Scrambler 2.3.1 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.1.4 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Scrambler on a vocal, drum loop, or effect. The defaults are `LOW` 300 Hz, `HIGH` 4.5 kHz, and `SCRAMBLE AMOUNT` 50%.
Set `LOW` and `HIGH` around the part of the spectrum you want to change. Everything outside that range stays as it is.
Raise `SCRAMBLE AMOUNT` until the sound is as unrecognisable as you want.
Try the factory presets: GENTLE OFFSET for subtle colour, BROKEN SPEECH for garbled voices, and TOTAL DISLOCATION for complete transformation.

rows: Previous and next preset, the preset list (factory preset groups and LOAD USER PRESET...; CUSTOM appears after a change), Save, Undo, and Redo.
The two edges of the scrambled range.
How strongly the range is scrambled.
First scramble point. Frequencies below the range pass through unchanged.
Second scramble point. Frequencies above the range pass through unchanged.
Dry/wet blend. 0% leaves the sound dry; 100% is fully formant-scrambled.

note.text: If LOW is set above HIGH, the two points are reordered, so the range always runs from the lower value to the higher one.

body.p: TB Scrambler divides the spectrum into 31 bands. In the bands between LOW and HIGH, the formant envelope and fine spectral structure are moved around with a fixed permutation, so the same settings always give the same result. The low end, rhythm, and overall energy are kept, which is why the result stays usable in a mix.

tip.text: Wider ranges destroy recognition faster but also blur the original rhythm and tone. For a subtle effect, keep the range narrow and the amount low.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows, or open the list to choose a factory or user preset. LOAD USER PRESET... opens a .tbscrambler file, and Save stores the current settings as one. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a setting. Undo and Redo step through recent changes.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Disguised voice
recipes.use: A voice that keeps its rhythm but loses its identity.
steps: Keep the range inside the speech band so the timing stays readable.

recipes.title: Drum loop grit
recipes.use: Metallic colour on a loop without losing the groove.
steps: Raise AMOUNT slowly; small values already change the colour.

recipes.title: Alien transmission
steps: Follow with a band-pass EQ for an even narrower radio sound.

recipes.title: Bass that keeps its weight
recipes.use: Movement in the upper harmonics of a bass.
steps: Raise LOW above the fundamental if the bass loses weight.
